messages:
alex: Quick sanity check — running into a weird case where streaming rpcs drop right after a service identity refresh. Repro with python SDK (requests) and node (ws). Anyone else seen streaming disconnects tied to token rotation?

maria: Hmm not off the top of my head. Which auth flow are you using — short-lived SA tokens or an OIDC exchange?

alex: We mint short-lived tokens via our OIDC SA bridge per-project. Token TTL ~10m. The stream is established, then a minute before expiry we fetch a new token and call the SDK's refresh hook, but the socket closes within a few seconds.

sam: This sounds like a connection-level auth header mismatch. Some clients don't hot-swap Authorization on the wire. Node ws will close if server rejects a message with old token. Python requests streaming sometimes keeps writing and then gets 401 mid-stream.

alex: Log snippet: ```
INFO 2026-02-12 18:12:03 stream_id=abc123 token_refresh start
INFO 2026-02-12 18:12:04 stream_id=abc123 token_refresh done new_exp=1670000000
WARN 2026-02-12 18:12:06 stream_id=abc123 recv: 401 Unauthorized
ERROR 2026-02-12 18:12:06 stream_id=abc123 connection closed by peer
```

maria: Two quick ideas: 1) rotate tokens earlier (refresh window >= 2x RTT) so there isn't an auth gap, 2) switch to a short-lived session key exchange where you perform a lightweight rehandshake instead of swapping headers mid-stream.

lena: FWIW, PR #3892 in our SDK adds a `rebindAuth()` callback for streaming transports — it attempts a graceful re-auth handshake. alex, can you try the branch? @sam implemented the node behavior.

sam: Also check that your proxy/nginx isn’t caching/rewriting Authorization and terminating the keepalive. We saw a similar pattern where the LB held the old token on the backend.

alex: Will try the PR branch. If it fails I can attach a minimal repro. One more nuance: python SDK uses `requests` with chunked transfer and doesn't expose a reconnect hook easily. Any pattern to patch in rebind?

maria: For python we added a wrapper that detects 401 frames and then calls `connection.reconnect()` with the new token in the headers. Ugly but effective. Code sketch: ```python
if resp.status_code == 401:
    new_token = token_provider.refresh()
    s.close()
    s = open_stream(headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {new_token}"})
```

lena: That's what the `rebindAuth()` does under the hood but keeps the socket lifecycle in the SDK so app code doesn't need to manage it. It also exposes backoff and jitter for reconnects.

alex: Great — trying the branch now. Quick question for SDK reviewers: when implementing rebind, should we require the auth provider to return a `renew_before` window so SDK can schedule refreshes, or just expose `refresh()` and let apps decide?

sam: Prefer provider returns `expires_at` / `renew_before` so SDK can do policy-based refresh (e.g., refresh at 20% of TTL). Less footguns for apps.

maria: Agreed. We should also document language-specific caveats (python chunked vs node ws vs java http2). I'll add a short doc section to the SDK repo.

alex: Pinging @lena and @sam for code review on the PR once CI passes. If folks see an obvious gap in the rebind approach LMs please shout now.

infra-bot: CI queued for branch feature/rebind-auth (build #1248) :rocket:

lena: If CI passes I'll merge and cut a 0.8.1 release. We'll add a migration note about enabling `auth.rebind=true` in config.

alex: Thanks all — I'll post a minimal repro if the branch doesn't fix it. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
